company.name: Jaiprakash Power Ventures Ltd
company.about: Jaiprakash Power Ventures runs 2,220 MW of power plants: the 1,320 MW Nigrie supercritical thermal plant and the 500 MW Bina thermal plant in Madhya Pradesh, and the 400 MW Vishnuprayag hydro plant in Uttarakhand, plus a 2 MTPA cement grinding unit at Nigrie. It sells power to state distribution companies under long-term agreements and on the power exchanges. Adani Power holds 24%, bought in May 2026 from the former promoter Jaiprakash Associates, which is in insolvency.

events.title: Stock falls 6.6% to ₹13.93 after Q2 results, then extends a three-day slide of about 9.5%
events.details: In the first session after the Q2 FY27 results (20 October was a market holiday), the shares fell about 6.6% to close at ₹13.93 on heavy volume of about 5.6 crore shares, roughly four times results-day volume. They fell again on 22 October to around ₹13.6–13.7, about 9.5% lower over three sessions and only a few percent above the 52-week low of ₹13.15. The stock traded below all its main moving averages, and no company news explained the extra selling.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the price is now about 25% below the ₹18.20 a share Adani Power paid for its 24% stake in May, which keeps the stake-increase question in focus.

events.title: Q2 FY27: revenue up 5% to ₹1,512 Cr, but PAT falls 82% to ₹33 Cr after ₹511 Cr NARCL charge
events.details: Revenue from operations for the September 2026 quarter rose 5.1% year on year to ₹1,512.12 crore but fell 14.8% from the June quarter. Profit after tax dropped to ₹33.34 crore from ₹182.10 crore after an exceptional charge of ₹511 crore for the settlement with NARCL. Profit before exceptional items and tax was about ₹521 crore; finance costs fell 16% and other income rose 67%. The auditors' review stayed qualified over the ₹5,696.51 crore lenders' recompense claim. The company held no earnings call.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: underlying earnings held up, but the headline loss of profit and the remaining legacy claims weighed on the stock.

events.title: Board names Jigar Dalal as CFO and Paresh Patel as company secretary after September retirements
events.details: With the Q2 results, the board appointed Jigar Dalal as chief financial officer from 1 November 2026 and Paresh Patel as company secretary from 1 December 2026. They replace R.K. Porwal and Mahesh Chaturvedi, who retired on 30 September. The company still has no chairman since Manoj Gaur resigned in July, and no managing director and CEO since Suren Jain resigned in May.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: filling the finance roles reduces the leadership gap, but the top jobs remain vacant five months after Adani Power took its stake.

events.title: September exchange power prices double year on year to ₹7.3/unit; coal e-auction premiums hit 94%
events.details: Data published in early October showed the average day-ahead price on IEX in September 2026 at ₹7.3 a unit, up 105% year on year, and the real-time market at ₹6.9, up 108%. The July–September quarter averaged ₹5.7, up 46%. India's September power use rose 11.35% to 162.19 billion units. At the same time, Coal India's September e-auction cleared at a 94% premium to notified prices, up from 59% in August.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: about 60% of Nigrie's output is sold at market prices, so higher power prices help, but the plant now buys more coal on the market after giving up its captive mine.

events.title: Adani Power calls report that it will raise its stake to 51% 'completely incorrect'
events.details: A media report in September 2026 said the Adani group was considering raising its holding in Jaiprakash Power Ventures to 51%, which would trigger an open offer to other shareholders. Adani Power described the report as completely incorrect. Adani Power holds 24%, just under the 25% level that requires an open offer under takeover rules, and about 79% of that block is pledged to the company's lenders.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the denial removed a near-term takeover premium that some investors had priced in.

events.title: Agrees ₹511 Cr full and final settlement of NARCL's insolvency claim; shares jump up to 14%
events.details: Jaiprakash Power Ventures agreed to pay ₹511 crore to National Asset Reconstruction Company (NARCL) in full and final settlement of its Section 7 insolvency petition, which related to corporate guarantees the company gave for loans of its former parent Jaiprakash Associates. The settlement depends on definitive agreements and payment, after which the petition is to be withdrawn. Sources differ on whether it was disclosed on 19 or 21 September. The shares rose 10–14% on 21 September, touching ₹17.48. The full amount was charged in Q2 FY27.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: settling removes an insolvency threat to the company, but the larger ₹5,697 crore recompense claim from ICICI-led lenders is still open.

events.title: CRISIL keeps BBB rating on ₹5,600 Cr of bank loans on Watch Negative over the NARCL case
events.details: CRISIL Ratings kept its BBB rating on ₹5,600 crore of the company's bank facilities on Rating Watch with Negative Implications, tying the watch to the NARCL insolvency petition then before the tribunal. CRISIL expected the Bina plant to run at about 74–75% load and debt to keep falling. Earlier in the year, India Ratings withdrew its rating at the company's request, and Acuité had the company at BBB+ on Watch Developing.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the rating outcome hinged on the NARCL case, which the company moved to settle three weeks later.

events.title: Q1 FY27: revenue up 12% to ₹1,776 Cr, PAT up 69% to ₹469 Cr despite ₹194 Cr coal-mine charge
events.details: For the June 2026 quarter, consolidated revenue rose 12.2% year on year to ₹1,775.70 crore and profit after tax rose 68.6% to ₹468.84 crore. Results included a ₹193.63 crore exceptional charge for surrendering the Amelia (North) and Bandha North coal mines, and a net tax credit of about ₹92 crore from moving to the lower corporate tax regime. Operating margin was about 42.7%, against 8.8% in the March quarter, helped by strong summer demand and high exchange prices.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the quarter showed how much profit swings with merchant power prices; part of the profit came from a one-time tax gain.

events.title: Adani Power discloses 17.5% of JPVL pledged to the company's lenders, plus 1.5% under a non-disposal pact
events.details: Adani Power revised its encumbrance disclosure for the Jaiprakash Power Ventures shares it bought in May. 120.05 crore shares, 17.52% of the company, are pledged and 10.22 crore shares, 1.49%, are under a non-disposal undertaking, in favour of IDBI and the lender groups of the Nigrie and Vishnuprayag plants, with IDBI Trusteeship as trustee. Together that is about 79% of Adani Power's 24% holding. The pledge carries over security that lenders held on the former promoter's stake.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the pledge is security for the company's own loans rather than a sign of stress at Adani Power, but it ties up most of the block.

events.title: Chairman Manoj Gaur resigns, ending the Jaypee group founders' presence on the board
events.details: Manoj Gaur, of the family that founded the Jaypee group, resigned as non-executive chairman and director on 6 July 2026. Days earlier, on 1 July, Shruti Anup Shah and Jayant Misra joined as independent directors as several long-serving independent directors left. In late July the annual general meeting approved all 11 resolutions, including the regularisation of the directors nominated by Adani Power. No dividend was declared.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the board is now shaped by Adani Power, but no new chairman had been named by October.

events.title: MD & CEO Suren Jain and four other directors resign; three Adani Power nominees join the board
events.details: A day after Adani Power bought the 24% stake, the board accepted five resignations, including managing director and CEO Suren Jain and vice-chairman Sunil Kumar Sharma. Three Adani Power nominees were appointed: Savan Jayendra Patel as whole-time director, and Jayadeb Nanda and Naresh Telgu as non-executive directors. No replacement managing director or CEO was named, and by October 2026 the post was still vacant. Former Jaypee group directors continued to leave in the following weeks, ending with chairman Manoj Gaur's resignation in July.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: management control passed from the Jaypee group to Adani Power's nominees, which could bring operating and funding benefits but also related-party questions.

events.title: Adani Power buys former promoter's 24% stake for ₹2,994 Cr, about ₹18.20 a share
events.details: Under the tribunal-approved resolution plan for Jaiprakash Associates, Adani Power acquired its entire 24% stake in Jaiprakash Power Ventures, 164.48 crore shares, for ₹2,993.59 crore, about ₹18.20 a share. The deal was exempt from an open offer because it formed part of the insolvency plan and stayed below 25%. Adani Power also agreed to buy Jaiprakash Associates' 180 MW Churk power plant and other assets, taking the total package to about ₹4,194 crore. The company became an associate of Adani Power.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a large, well-funded power company replacing an insolvent promoter is the main reason to own the stock, though minority holders got no open offer.

events.title: Board decides to surrender Amelia (North) and Bandha North coal mines, ending captive coal for Nigrie
events.details: The board approved surrendering the Amelia (North) and Bandha North coal blocks in Singrauli, citing recent government policy changes and concerns about viability. Amelia (North), with 3.92 million tonnes a year of capacity, had supplied the 1,320 MW Nigrie plant. The surrender needs government and lender approvals. The company took a ₹193.63 crore exceptional charge in Q1 FY27 and said any compensation would be booked on settlement and was not expected to be material.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: Nigrie now depends on linkage and market coal, so fuel costs, not just power prices, will drive its margins.

events.title: FY26: profit falls to ₹451 Cr as Q4 swings to a ₹13 Cr loss; auditors issue a qualified opinion
events.details: Consolidated profit for FY26 was ₹450.63 crore on sales of ₹5,563.46 crore; standalone profit fell to ₹441.5 crore from ₹810.7 crore. The March 2026 quarter showed a consolidated loss of ₹13.37 crore against a ₹155.67 crore profit a year earlier, with operating margin down to about 8.8%, which the pipeline links to weaker merchant power prices. Auditors Lodha & Co. gave modified opinions, citing the lenders' ₹5,696.51 crore recompense claim, which is not provided for, and the carrying value of MAT credit.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: two weak quarters in a row showed how exposed the company is to market power prices, and the audit qualifications flag unresolved legacy liabilities.

events.title: NCLAT dismisses Vedanta's challenge to Adani's plan for former promoter Jaiprakash Associates
events.details: The appellate tribunal dismissed Vedanta's appeal against the approval of Adani Enterprises' resolution plan for Jaiprakash Associates, the insolvent former promoter that held 24% of Jaiprakash Power Ventures. The Supreme Court had earlier declined to interfere at the interim stage. The ruling cleared the way for Adani to pay the first instalment of about ₹6,000 crore to lenders and for Adani Power to take over the 24% stake later in May.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: removing the legal challenge settled who would own the largest block of the company's shares.

events.title: NCLT approves Adani Enterprises' ₹14,535 Cr plan for Jaiprakash Associates, the 24% holder
events.details: The Allahabad bench of the National Company Law Tribunal orally approved Adani Enterprises' resolution plan for Jaiprakash Associates on 17 March 2026, against admitted creditor claims of about ₹57,185 crore. Jaiprakash Associates' own shareholders get nothing under the plan. Because Jaiprakash Associates owned 24% of Jaiprakash Power Ventures, the approval set up the transfer of that stake to the Adani group, which was completed in May through Adani Power.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a key step in ending the uncertainty over the company's insolvent promoter.

events.title: Q3 FY26: profit collapses 97% to ₹3.8 Cr on flat revenue; shares fall more than 7% next day
events.details: For the December 2025 quarter, consolidated revenue was ₹1,155.57 crore, up 1.4% year on year but down about 20% from the September quarter. Profit after tax fell to ₹3.77 crore from ₹126.68 crore a year earlier. Pre-tax profit was only ₹18.62 crore and the effective tax rate was about 80%. Operating margin fell to about 15% from 32.7% in the previous quarter. The shares rose 4.3% to ₹16.11 on results day but fell more than 7% on 5 February.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the first of two weak quarters that showed how quickly merchant-price swings can wipe out profit.

events.title: Adani Enterprises wins creditor vote for Jaiprakash Associates, owner of 24% of JPVL
events.details: Lenders to Jaiprakash Associates chose Adani Enterprises' resolution plan, worth about ₹14,535 crore, with about 89% of creditor votes, over a higher-headline but more deferred bid from Vedanta. Other bidders included Dalmia Cement, Jindal Power and PNC Infratech. Because Jaiprakash Associates held 24% of Jaiprakash Power Ventures, the vote made the Adani group the likely new owner of that block. Vedanta later challenged the outcome in the tribunals.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the result pointed to a strong strategic holder replacing an insolvent promoter, which the market had been speculating on since July 2025.

events.details: For the September 2025 quarter, consolidated sales were ₹1,438.3 crore, up from ₹1,226.4 crore a year earlier, while profit after tax was ₹182.10 crore, down 0.3%. Operating margin was about 32.7%, about the same as a year earlier. The June 2025 quarter had produced a profit of ₹278.13 crore, down about 20% year on year. events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a steady quarter before the sharp profit drop in the December and March quarters.

events.title: ICICI-led lenders look to sell ₹3,800 Cr of JPVL convertible preference shares in the market
events.details: Business Standard reported that ICICI Bank and other lenders were seeking buyers for compulsorily convertible preference shares in Jaiprakash Power Ventures with a face value of about ₹3,800 crore, received in a 2019–20 debt restructuring, by selling them in the open market. A banking source said a sale was premature while the insolvency of the former promoter was unresolved. The preference shares, if converted, would add a large number of equity shares. ICICI Bank later cut its equity holding from 9.97% to 4.57% in the June 2026 quarter.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the convertible shares are a lasting supply overhang and a source of dilution for equity holders.

events.title: Stock surges 44% in seven sessions to a 12-year high on talk of Adani bid for parent
events.details: Jaiprakash Power Ventures shares rose about 44% in seven trading days from ₹18.67 on 3 July 2025, reaching their highest level since May 2013; on 7 July alone they jumped 16% to ₹21.95 on heavy volume. Aggregators put the 52-week high at about ₹23.8–24.9 in this period. The rally followed media reports that the Adani group was the top bidder for Jaiprakash Associates, which owned 24% of the company. The company told the exchanges there was no unpublished price-sensitive information behind the move.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the stock began trading on takeover expectations here, and those highs have not been regained since.

events.title: SEBI fines company and top executives ₹54 lakh for misstated accounts; shares fall over 3%
events.details: SEBI's adjudicating officer fined Jaiprakash Power Ventures ₹14 lakh and its chairman Manoj Gaur, MD and CEO Suren Jain, two executive directors, the CFO and a former director ₹6–7 lakh each, ₹54 lakh in total. The order found the accounts for FY19 to FY21 were misstated through faulty accounting of corporate guarantees and related-party transactions, including an undisclosed US$150 million guarantee to State Bank of India. The company appealed to the Securities Appellate Tribunal. The shares fell more than 3% after the order.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the order highlighted the guarantees given for the former parent's debt, the same exposure behind later insolvency claims.

events.title: Promoter Jaiprakash Associates, holder of 24%, is admitted to insolvency by NCLT Allahabad
events.details: The Allahabad bench of the NCLT admitted the insolvency petition against Jaiprakash Associates, filed by ICICI Bank and later joined by State Bank of India, on 3 June 2024. The board of Jaiprakash Associates was suspended and an interim resolution professional took charge; the appellate tribunal declined to stay the process. Jaiprakash Associates held 24% of Jaiprakash Power Ventures, and the power company had given guarantees for some of its loans.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the promoter's insolvency put the company's ownership in play and exposed it to guarantee claims, both of which drove the stock for the next two years.

events.title: FY24: consolidated profit reaches about ₹1,022 Cr as revenue from operations rises to ₹6,763 Cr
events.details: The board approved audited FY24 results on 27 April 2024. Consolidated profit was about ₹1,021.9 crore and revenue from operations rose to about ₹6,763 crore from ₹5,787 crore in FY23. Sources describe the profit as including one-off items, though the breakdown was not found. Later comparisons put FY25 total consolidated revenue lower, at about ₹5,708 crore, and FY25 standalone profit at about ₹811 crore. The FY24 figures came while the former promoter, Jaiprakash Associates, was weeks away from being admitted to insolvency.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: FY24 was the recent peak; later years have earned far less, so it is not a guide to normal profit.
